EFBMC Example

Example R markdown notebook demonstrating workflow for EFBMC. Example notebook demonstrating workflow for EFBMC. We will demonstrate this method calibrating a simulated data set

Code locations for required R packages not on CRAN:

  1. impala
  2. mvBayes

Setup

First we need to import the required packages and make a useful function for the data

library(impala)
library(mvBayes)
library(BASS)
library(fdasrvf)
library(bayesplot)
library(coda)
library(readr)
library(interp)

make_matrix <- function(df,rownames = NULL){
  my_matrix <-  as.matrix(df)
  if(!is.null(rownames))
    rownames(my_matrix) = rownames
  my_matrix
}

Data Pre-Processing

We will simulate a simple toy data set with parameters

f <- function(x) {
  dnorm(seq(0, 1, length.out = 99),
        sin(2 * pi * x[1] ^ 2) / 4 - x[1] / 10 + 0.5,
        0.05) * x[2]
}

n = 100
M = 99
p = 3
sim_variables = matrix(runif(n * p), n)
x_test = matrix(runif(1000 * p), 1000)
e = rnorm(n * 99)
f_sim = matrix(0, n, M)
for (i in 1:n) {
  f_sim[i, ] = f(sim_variables[i, ])
}
y_test = matrix(0, 1000, M)
for (i in 1:1000) {
  y_test[i, ] = f(x_test[i, ])
}

Next we will generate the observation (experiment)

x_true = c(0.1028, 0.5930)
tt = seq(0, 1, length.out = M)
f_exp = f(x_true)

Look at the original data with the experiment overlaid

matplot(tt, t(f_sim), type = "l", col = "gray")
lines(tt, f_exp, col = "black")
legend(
  x = 0,
  y = 8,
  legend = c("simulation", "experiment"),
  col = c("gray", "black"),
  lty = 1
)

Elastic Functional Alignment

We will now align the computer model output to the experiment. We will need the aligned data ftilde_train and the shooting vectors vv_train. Additionally we will need the shooting vector for the experiment. In this case, since we are aligning to the experiment warping function will be identity (\(\gamma_{id}\)) and then the corresponding shooting vector vv_obs.

There is the option of the parameter lambda in multiple_align_functions that restricts the amount of alignment. In some cases we will set this to a small value (e.g., 0.01) to remove heteroskedacity from the warping functions.

tt = seq(0, 1, length.out = M)
warp_list = multiple_align_functions(
  t(f_sim),
  tt,
  f_exp,
  lambda = .01,
  parallel = TRUE,
  showplot = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)
gam_sim = warp_list$warping_functions
vv_sim = gam_to_psi(warp_list$warping_functions)
ftilde_sim = warp_list$fn

vv_obs = gam_to_psi(seq(0, 1, length.out=M))
gam_obs = seq(0, 1, length.out=M)
ftilde_obs = f_exp

We will now plot the alignment results. First is the aligned functions.

matplot(tt, ftilde_sim, type = "l", col = "gray")
lines(tt, ftilde_obs, col = "black")
legend(
  x = 0,
  y = 8,
  legend = c("simulation", "experiment"),
  col = c("gray", "black"),
  lty = 1
)

Then the corresponding warping functions

matplot(tt, gam_sim, type = "l", col = "gray")
lines(tt, gam_obs, col = "black")
legend(
  x = 0,
  y = 8,
  legend = c("simulation", "experiment"),
  col = c("gray", "black"),
  lty = 1
)

and the corresponding shooting vectors

matplot(tt, vv_sim, type = "l", col = "gray")
lines(tt, vv_obs, col = "black")
legend(
  x = 0,
  y = 8,
  legend = c("simulation", "experiment"),
  col = c("gray", "black"),
  lty = 1
)

Surrogate Model Fitting

Next, we will fit the BASS surrogate to the computer model and evaluate its performance. We use the mvBayes package due to its ability to introspect surrogates and their performance.

The choice of nBasis here is made from exploratory data analysis. It can also be chosen based on the percentage of variance explained from the functional principal component analysis (fPCA) decomposition. The parameter in mvBayes do perform this is propVarExplained.

emu_ftilde = mvBayes(
  bass,
  sim_variables,
  t(ftilde_sim)
  )
## Starting mvBayes with 1 components, using 1 cores.
## MCMC Start #-- Aug 26 17:45:56 --# nbasis: 0 
## MCMC iteration 1000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:57 --# nbasis: 3 
## MCMC iteration 2000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:57 --# nbasis: 3 
## MCMC iteration 3000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:57 --# nbasis: 3 
## MCMC iteration 4000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:57 --# nbasis: 3 
## MCMC iteration 5000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:57 --# nbasis: 3 
## MCMC iteration 6000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:57 --# nbasis: 3 
## MCMC iteration 7000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:57 --# nbasis: 3 
## MCMC iteration 8000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:57 --# nbasis: 3 
## MCMC iteration 9000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:57 --# nbasis: 3 
## MCMC iteration 10000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:58 --# nbasis: 3
## Generating 'samples' attribute, since it was absent in 'bmList[[1]]'
## Approximating 'residSD', since 'residSDExtract' is None
emu_vv = mvBayes(
  bass,
  sim_variables,
  t(vv_sim),
  basisType="pns"
)
## ℹ Setting n.pc to 2...
## Initial PNS subsphere dimension 3 
## Percentage of variability in PNS sequence 99.26 
## Percent explained by 1st three PNS scores out of total variability: 
##  98.9 0.36 NA
## Starting mvBayes with 1 components, using 1 cores.
## MCMC Start #-- Aug 26 17:45:58 --# nbasis: 0 
## MCMC iteration 1000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:58 --# nbasis: 7 
## MCMC iteration 2000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:58 --# nbasis: 9 
## MCMC iteration 3000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:59 --# nbasis: 7 
## MCMC iteration 4000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:59 --# nbasis: 6 
## MCMC iteration 5000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:59 --# nbasis: 6 
## MCMC iteration 6000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:59 --# nbasis: 6 
## MCMC iteration 7000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:59 --# nbasis: 6 
## MCMC iteration 8000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:59 --# nbasis: 6 
## MCMC iteration 9000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:59 --# nbasis: 6 
## MCMC iteration 10000 #-- Aug 26 17:45:59 --# nbasis: 6

We can examine the fit of the surrogate model by looking at mvBayes diagnostic plots. We want to examine the MSE and if it is reasonable as well as the \(R^2\) value to make sure its high enough. Also we can use the lower right panel to see how much explained variance is contained in the 7 principal components.

plot(emu_ftilde)
## Warning in predict.mvBayes(object, Xtest, returnPostCoefs = TRUE, idxSamples =
## idxSamples): 'idxSamples' is not an argument of the bayesModel predict
## function...setting idxSamples='default'

We can also examine the fPCA decomposition to explore it more further if needed. We see that 7 components contain 99% of the explained variance

plot(emu_ftilde$basisInfo)

Lets evaluate the shooting vector emulator

plot(emu_vv)
## Warning in predict.mvBayes(object, Xtest, returnPostCoefs = TRUE, idxSamples =
## idxSamples): 'idxSamples' is not an argument of the bayesModel predict
## function...setting idxSamples='default'

Bayesian Model Calibration

We will now set up impala to perform the calibration. First we need to setup the parameter names and bounds on the parameters. impala sets uniform priors on the parameters based on their bounds.

input_names = c('X1','X2','X3')
bounds = list()
for (i in 1:p){
  bounds[[input_names[i]]] = c(min(sim_variables[,i]), max(sim_variables[,i]))
}

We will now set up the calibration object and add the experimental data for the aligned data and shooting vectors. impala is set up to run multiple chains and do annealing so we set up a temperature ladder of 20 chains. We also set the chains to run for 4000 samples with a burn in of 2000 samples. The last line runs the calibration.

setup = CalibSetup(bounds, cf_bounds)
    
model_ftilde = ModelmvBayes(emu_ftilde, input_names)
model_vv = ModelmvBayes(emu_vv, input_names)

setup = addVecExperiments(setup, t(ftilde_obs), model_ftilde, 0.001, 20, rep(1, M))
setup = addVecExperiments(setup, t(vv_obs), model_vv, 0.01, 20, rep(1, M))

setup = setTemperatureLadder(setup, 1.05 ^ (0:19))
setup = setMCMC(setup, 4000, 2000, 1, 10)
out_cal = calibPool(setup)

Next we will extract the parameters for the last 2000 samples and thin by 1.

uu = seq(2000, 4000, 2)

theta = tran_unif(out_cal$theta[uu, 1, ], setup$bounds_mat, names(setup$bounds))

time_new = seq(0, 1, length.out = M)

ftilde_pred_obs = evalm(setup$models[[1]], theta)
vv_pred_obs = evalm(setup$models[[2]], theta)
gam_pred_obs = psi_to_gam(t(vv_pred_obs))

Now we will look at the likelihood and chains to make sure the MCMC chains are stable and have converged.

plot(out_cal$llik, type="l", ylab="Log-Likelihood", xlab="Iteration")

Next we will look at convergence diagnostics of ESS and \(\hat{R}\)

samps_coda = list()
for (ii in 1:20){
  samps_coda[[ii]] = mcmc(out_cal$theta[uu,ii,])
}
samps_coda_all = mcmc.list(samps_coda)
effectiveSize(samps_coda_all) 
##       var1       var2       var3 
##   90.06345 1554.23073 6255.76304
gelman.diag(samps_coda_all)
## Potential scale reduction factors:
## 
##      Point est. Upper C.I.
## [1,]      1.000          1
## [2,]      1.002          1
## [3,]      0.999          1
## 
## Multivariate psrf
## 
## 1
samps = data.frame(theta)
mcmc_trace(samps)

Examine the pair plot of the parameters. The diagonal contains the posterior distributions of the parameters. The off diagonal is the dependence.

p = mcmc_pairs(samps, off_diag_fun="hex", diag_fun = "dens")
## Warning: Only one chain in 'x'. This plot is more useful with multiple chains.
p

mcmc_hist(samps)
## `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`.

Next we are going to evaluate the surrogate model at the calibrate parameters for the entire posterior distribution. They gray curves are the computer model, blue curves are the calibrated surrogate curves, and black is the experiment.

matplot(
  time_new,
  ftilde_sim,
  type = "l",
  col = "gray",
  lty = 1
)
matplot(
  time_new,
  t(ftilde_pred_obs),
  type = "l",
  col = "lightblue",
  lty = 1,
  add = TRUE
)
lines(time_new, ftilde_obs, col = "black")
legend(
  "bottomright",
  legend = c("simulation", "prediction", "experiment"),
  col = c("gray", "lightblue", "black"),
  lty = 1
)

matplot(
  time_new,
  vv_sim,
  type = "l",
  col = "gray",
  lty = 1
)
matplot(
  time_new,
  t(vv_pred_obs),
  type = "l",
  col = "lightblue",
  lty = 1,
  add = TRUE
)
lines(time_new, vv_obs, col = "black")
legend(
  "bottomright",
  legend = c("simulation", "prediction", "experiment"),
  col = c("gray", "lightblue", "black"),
  lty = 1
)

matplot(
  time_new,
  gam_sim,
  type = "l",
  col = "gray",
  lty = 1
)
matplot(
  time_new,
  gam_pred_obs,
  type = "l",
  col = "lightblue",
  lty = 1,
  add = TRUE
)
lines(time_new, gam_obs, col = "black")
legend(
  "bottomright",
  legend = c("simulation", "prediction", "experiment"),
  col = c("gray", "lightblue", "black"),
  lty = 1
)

We then combine the outputs of the emulators via composition to look at in the original data space

obspred = matrix(0, M, length(uu))
for (i in 1:length(uu)) {
  obspred[, i] = warp_f_gamma(ftilde_pred_obs[i, ], time_new, invertGamma(gam_pred_obs[, i]))
}

matplot(
    tt,
    t(f_sim),
    type = "l",
    col = "gray",
    lty = 1
  )
matplot(
  tt,
  obspred ,
  type = "l",
  col = "lightblue",
  lty = 1,
  add = TRUE
)
lines(tt, f_exp, col = "black")
legend(
  "bottomright",
  legend = c("simulation", "prediction", "experiment"),
  col = c("gray", "lightblue", "black"),
  lty = 1
)

Sensitivity Analysis

We can also perform sensitivity analysis on the surrogate through mvBayes by doing the following. The BASS emulator has a closed form sobol indices and we will utilize that. mvBayes also provides the ability to monte carlo to determine the sobol indices.

First we will look at the amplitude surrogate

out_ftilde = mvBayes::mvSobol(emu_ftilde)
## Start ##------ Tue Apr 28 15:35:17 2026 ------## 
## Integrating ##------ Tue Apr 28 15:35:17 2026 ------## 
## Shuffling ##------ Tue Apr 28 15:35:18 2026 ------## 
## Finish ##------ Tue Apr 28 15:35:18 2026 ------##
## Warning in mvBayes::mvSobol(emu_ftilde): 'BASS' has not implemented totalOrder
plot(out_ftilde, labels=input_names)
## Warning in plot.sobol(out_ftilde, labels = input_names): 'object' does not have
## totalOrderSobol

Next the phase surrogate

out_vv = mvBayes::mvSobol(emu_vv, nMC=2^8)
## Warning in predict.mvBayes(structure(list(X = structure(c(0.747553555993363, :
## 'idxSamples' is not an argument of the bayesModel predict function...setting
## idxSamples='default'
plot(out_vv, labels=input_names)

We can also look at sensitivity as a functional boxplot or waterfall plot

plot(out_ftilde, labels=input_names, waterfall=TRUE)
## Warning in plot.sobol(out_ftilde, labels = input_names, waterfall = TRUE):
## 'object' does not have totalOrderSobol
